name: CSR Benchmark (Conditional Semantic Rate)
description: This work presents the CSR Benchmark (Conditional Semantic Rate), an experimental study testing the hypothesis that the minimum message size () required to reconstruct a correct answer is a decreasing function of the decoder's prior knowledge (), while maintaining constant accuracy. We compared five levels of decoder prior knowledge ( bits) across three world complexities ( bits), totaling 150 runs with 10 random seeds each, on an NVIDIA RTX 3060 GPU. We used a VAE architecture with a 4-dimensional continuous bottleneck and L2 regularization on the mean to force real compression. Results demonstrate that for , the message L2 norm drops from () to (), a 68.6% reduction, while maintaining 100% accuracy. For , we observe a phase transition: accuracy is perfect at and , but unstable at (mean 81.6%, high variance). For , the architecture reaches its limit at partial . The metric bits confirms that the message carries only information relevant to the answer, eliminating the "Mean Collapse" phenomenon observed in earlier experiment versions. This work provides the first empirical evidence that conditional semantic compression to the decoder works, but exhibits a phase transition when prior knowledge crosses the sufficiency threshold, with instability in partial knowledge regions.
